column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check

The article gives c. 480-408 BC for his life, and also says he helped rebuild Miletus in 479 BC and that Strabo credited him with Rhodes in 408 BC, when he would have been very old; Rhodes is therefore given as 'said to', no date. The article says he planned the Piraeus 'for Pericles' and also dates a Piraeus study to 451 BC; neither date printed. Left out: patent-law claim, the polynomial pumping formulas, Theano's treatise.

The article says the Huneric-Eudocia marriage alliance was already made in 442 when she was four years old, and also that they married in 455 or 456; the 442 betrothal left out. The article says he lifted persecution early in the reign and also that the 484 persecution began later; the entry's 'harshest persecution in 484' is respected. Left out: Victor of Vita's account of his death, which the article says may be a later addition; the cutting off of tongues and right hands at Tipasa.

The article describes the flight to Aretas and the Nabataean siege twice in two sections; told once. Gregory Doudna's 2013 proposal that Hyrcanus II was the Teacher of Righteousness left out. The article gives ethnarch 'probably 47-40 BCE' and brief kingship 67-66 BCE; the span not printed.

The article gives the Battle of al-Buhayra as May or 14 April 1130; no day given. Whether he met al-Ghazali is disputed in the article (hagiographers say yes, Ibn Khallikan and modern historians doubt); stated only that he came under al-Ghazali's influence, which the article states. The article says Abd al-Mu'min was elected in 1133 in the lead but describes the succession as uncertain; no year given for his accession. Left out: the legends of the ship, the buried men, the cave pilgrimage.

The article says she was 14 in 1184 (she would be 14 by the entry's birth year 1170; consistent) but calls Philip 15 at the 1180 marriage; no ages beyond that printed. The article says she died the day after the twins were born (15 March) but also has the second twin dying on 17 March, three days after birth: both given as the article has them. The entry says Artois 'passed to the French crown'; the text says it returned when Louis became king, as the article.

The entry says he defeated Amr in 900 as governor for the caliph; the article says the caliph did not formally recognise him at first and then invested him after the battle: told as the article has it. The article says the Samanid campaigns of 900-901 under Muhammad ibn Harun and Ismail's son Ahmad followed; left out. Mausoleum not mentioned in the article, so not mentioned.

The entry says he was crowned tsar after defeating Byzantine armies; the article says Theodor was crowned Peter in 1185 and Asen became co-ruler in 1187 or 1188, so the text gives only the co-rulership. The article's lead says 1187/1188 for his rule, 'nine years' from Akropolites. Left out: the tax details, ethnic theories beyond the first paragraph, the Cuman warrior's capture of Komnenos.

The article gives his birth as the 1190s (between 1192 and 1196). Death date uncertain in the article (24 June 1241 per Vásáry, or May/June; Akropolites); the text follows Madgearu. The entry says Melnik was absorbed; the article does not mention Melnik, so not printed. The article says Akropolites had Boril besieged seven years, which modern historians think a confusion of months and years: left out.

The article is partly self-contradictory on the dates of the presidency (1978 to 1989) and on 'Hartal' etc.; only firm dates used. The entry says prime minister in 1977; the article says 1977-1978. Left out: the 1953 Hartal, the Siyarata poem, the pardon of Gonawala Sunil, the Lee Kuan Yew remark, the sports career detail, the Daily Telegraph quotation (the quote is disputed in tone; not verified beyond the article). The nickname and foreign policy left out.

The article says silver was found in 1512 and the village founded in 1516; the entry says the town was founded after silver was found in 1516. The text gives only the 1516 founding, no discovery year. The article itself dates the radon spring to 1864 and the first radon spa to 1906. Left out: the spa treatments (controversial), sports, transport, Radium Palace Hotel, notable people.

The article gives the Fuggerei as founded 1521 in its lead and 'beginning in 1516' in the foundations section; only 1516 and 1523 printed. The article says he lent money in 1500 for St Peter's, the Sistine Chapel; left out (ahistorical in places). The wealth estimate left out. The article puts the early years in Venice from 14; the 'cleric with prebends' left out.

SKIPPED: article has under about 250 words of substance (geography, tehsils, 2011 census figures, a medical college) and nothing on the Maratha principality or Baoni that the entry gives; a longer text would be padding The article is named after the town of Jalaun, once the headquarters of a Maratha governor; district area 4,565 km2, population 1,689,974 (2011 census). It has no history section.

The article's lead calls him the first European to trace the Nile upstream to the Blue Nile source, but also says Páez reached the source in 1618 and Lobo in 1629; the text does not claim he was first to the source, only first to trace the Blue Nile to its confluence (as the article says). Left out: Freemasonry, the Bruce Codex, Munchausen, his height, the Strates toast, the second marriage.
Length: article gives 348 miles (560 km), matching the entry. Left out: dams, bridges, tributary lists, sturgeon and catfish counts (dated survey), recreation details.

The article says he reigned 41 years; the entry says about forty and c. 786-746 BCE; the text says about four decades and cites Albright. Thiele's alternative dating (coregency 793-782, sole rule to 753) is not printed. The article dates the earthquake both c. 760 BC and 750 BC (in a quote); 'about 760 BCE' used. The article says a 2020 bulla claim is disputed as a forgery: left out. Thomas Römer's theory left out.

The article says the Joanna-Afonso marriage was annulled in 1478 and also that she renounced the Castilian title then; both told. It says she was 'forced to renounce' the title in 1478 and relinquished it again in 1522; both printed as 'renounced'/'relinquished'. Left out: the details of her mother's affair, the 1498 household, the 1504 marriage plan, fiction.

The entry says he was removed from office in 1980 months after the coup; the article says the coup prompted him to resign within six months. The text says 'prompted him to resign'. The article's first sentences say president 1975-1980. Left out: Dutch knighthood detail, wife's honour.

The article titles the 1721 book A Plan of Civil and Historical Architecture; the entry says Outline of Historical Architecture, so the text names no title. The article says the Karlskirche was 'started in 1715' in prose and 1716-23 in the list; 1715 printed. The article puts Joseph I's service in the 1690s although Joseph reigned later; the text follows its wording of the 1690 arches. Left out: the St John Nepomuk casket paragraph, the list of works, the Court Library and Schönbrunn (article lists Schönbrunn only as 1695 in the list).

The article gives his age as 70 at Belgrade, consistent with 1386 birth only roughly (69-70). Left out: the biographers, the missions in California and Texas (kept short), the date of the feast day changes, the bull of 1724.

The entry calls him Venezuela's first president; the article says Cristóbal Mendoza was named president in 1811 and Páez was the first head of government after the dissolution of Gran Colombia. The text says only that he became president in 1830. The article gives his second term as 1839-1842 and 1839-1843: the end of that term is left out. 1835 as the end of his first term is given in the article's lead. Left out: the Las Queseras date, epilepsy, the New York minister, the arts medal, Civilization VI.

Article gives no 1976 date for the Patriotic Front (desc does); article places it at Lancaster House 1979, so I gave no year for its formation. Article: Nkomo fled 1983; desc says driven from government 1982 (dismissal not stated in article); not contradicted.

Article's Early years has Gómez joining Castro in 1899 and becoming head of military in 1902 before VP posts; kept as article gives. Article is loose about airports and oil development timing; omitted.
Article gives Passion-Flowers as 1853 in text and 1854 in the works list; year omitted. Article gives the Mothers' Day Proclamation as 1870 and 1872; omitted.
Desc: 'driven' no; desc says Pavon 1861; article says indecisive battle September 1861 without naming Pavon; I left it unnamed. Article lead gives death 11 April 1870; not used.

Article says 2010 MW total while station figures after expansion sum higher; I printed the article's 2,010 MW and the expansion figures as separate sentences. Rehabilitation said scheduled to finish 2025 in the article; omitted completion claim. Desc says built 1955-1959; article opening 1960 given too.

Article gives Mihr Hormozd as executioner after volunteering; Khosrow executed 28 February 628. The article says the coup may have been 23/24 Feb; kept as given. Words attributed: Daryaee quoted as 'devastating effect' - fine.

Article gives the deposed king and queen detained and reportedly dead around 1981, Britannica counting Kaysone among those responsible; omitted as contested. Article's Family section runs to 2026 events; omitted.
Article's final demographics paragraph (2020 census) contains an impossible figure (21,813,334 for 2010); left out. Omitted 1965 and 2019 items as sourced thinly/contested.
Omitted the Tourism paragraph's vandalised sentences about the unseen attraction.

Article contradicts itself on the Raichur Doab: lead says 1512, Deccan section implies 1509 annexation, desc says 1520. Raichur Doab year left out; Raichur Fort 1520 given as article states. Yusuf Adil Shah's death (listed as open disagreement) left out. 'Yavana' title and Gulbarga omitted.
Desc mentions Margrave John of Brandenburg-Küstrin; not in article, so not in text.

Article says selection involves Shakya and Bajracharya castes; desc says Shakya only; I wrote 'Shakya and Bajracharya' (broader, not contradicting). Left out the royal massacre portent story and the 1984 Dhana Kumari removal.

Article gives Kashef's tea start as 1899 and 1900 and elsewhere in first attempts; year left out. Article's tea-industry decline section is a present assessment; left out. Desc says Karkiya dynasty capital and Ismail sheltered; not in article, not contradicted.
Article dates the tunnel 'around 395 BC'; desc says traditionally 398-397 BCE; no date given for the tunnel. Article also gives 406 BC flood and 393 BC prodigy.
Article's 1903 clash is with the Mullah's 'Dervish' scouts; omitted political-assessment passages of the Politics section. Desc and article agree on 2007 and Aug 2023.
Article's airport and gang statements omitted as present-day. Desc's Rigaud 1810-1811 southern government is not in article.
Desc says seat of one of the seven tenths of the Republic of Valais; the article does not mention it, so it is not in the text.
Desc covers Leip and 1915/1937; I did not repeat. Article lists Andersen's single sales at 700 copies before Belgrade; kept as stated.
Desc gives Free State Bottleneck 1919-1923; article gives only the proclamation of 10 January 1919 and no end date. Omitted the mayors list, politics and events calendar.
Omitted the 2007 Cryptosporidium outbreak details; its causes are the article's inference. Desc's O'Flaherty 13th-century story not in article.
Article gives 'Lusatia reintegrated with Poland early 13th century under Henry the Bearded' and a tangled 1319-1364 sequence; left out. Article has '1031-1031' typo; used 1031.
Article gives death c. 2334 BC, entry r. c. 2358-2334 BCE: no dates printed. Article's translations of the vase inscription differ (son of Ukush vs son of U-U); Ukush used.

Article says it was combined in the 5th century under Dhatusena; the entry says 5th or 6th century, so no century is given for the compilation. Article also dates Ashoka's missionaries 255 BCE vs Edict 13's 260 BCE; left out.
Article's reign account is partly promotional; kept to dated facts. Article says Panchayat 28 years vs entry 'three decades'; left out.

Article gives Maron as 350-410 (4th century) and the entry says 5th-century monk: no century given for Maron. Article contradicts itself on Monothelitism and communion; only stated that Maronites hold they were never out of communion.

Article gives death c. 1991 BCE; entry gives r. c. 1990 BCE: no date printed. Article says he fits a 7-year gap in the Turin Canon; entry says 'a few years': left out. A Lisht slate bowl once thought to name him was shown by Janosi not to; left out.
Article dates end 'late 238 or early 237' and surrender of Utica/Hippo late 238 or very early 237; entry says 238, so left unstated.
Article gives Merneptah's 5th year as 1208 BCE; consistent with entry.
Date c. 840 vs Lemaire's up to 810 mentioned as the article hedges. Details of the 7,000 killed at Nebo and the vessels of Jehovah left out (translation with lacunae).
Article calls him 'de facto military dictator'; heading 'In office' used.
Article's figures on Jewish victims conflict; only the USHMM population figure and 'estimates differ' used.
Article calls Yoritomo third son of 'Minamoto no Yoshimoto' (probably a slip for Yoshitomo); father left unnamed.
Birth: article says c. 1159 and also 'born just before the Heiji Rebellion in 1160'; entry says 1159, so no birth year printed.

Entry says Champa's last principality abolished 1832; article gives no year for Champa conquest, so none printed. Article says Cambodia incorporated 1834 and war with Siam 1833-34; Siamese invasion coincided with Khoi's revolt. 'in the account given' hedge because article asserts that causal line.
Entry gives no date; article's c. 1850 BCE is for the older material.
Article gives Videla as dictator 1976 to 1981; not stated. Article's names for the founders identified in 2005 differ from earlier ones; only Villaflor and Duquet named.
Entry says it became a defining feature of Seljuk architecture; article debates origins (Iraq vs NE Iran), so origins stated as scholars' views.
Article is short (about 280 words of substance). Entry mentions statues of Marduk carried off; not in article, so left out.

Entry gives Tariq crossing 711, Musa 712, recall 714; article gives only 713-714 for subordinate campaigns and no crossing year, so no years printed for the conquest. Entry says died 716; article 'about 715-716' used. 'Jebel Musa named for him' attributed per article to Ibn Battuta; hedged.
Article gives no year for Kadesh, so none printed.
Article's 'Since 2026' composition section is empty; omitted. Article says Prince Alexander I and Alexander Battenberg: same person, kept as given.

Entry says he 'served the Lê court' and 'led' the 1813 embassy; the article does not say either, so text says only 'trip to China in 1813' and the 1820 delegation. Article says Kiều circulated after 1813 per official biography; kept hedged.
Article gives 18 September for the Assinaros surrender and 3/9 September for the sea battles; Thucydides' figures for the fleet differ from Plutarch's; left out.

Article says Jämtland and Härjedalen were regained by Denmark-Norway in 1570, which contradicts the entry's 'no territory changed hands'; left out. Article's naval battle dates (30 May 1563 Bornholm vs 30 May 1564) conflict; left out. Article says Treaty made Denmark dominant power; entry says exhaustion; omitted.
Article says Duma/Manifesto promise 'no law without Duma approval'; kept. Entry says Nicholas 'consistently undermined the Duma'; text says only veto and dissolution powers.
Entry's description names the Electoral Palatinate, Counts of Erbach, Archbishop of Mainz; not in article, so not repeated. Article places Odenwald between Rhine plain, Main (entry also says Neckar).

Article gives annexation to Thracia as 45-46 AD, entry 46 CE: text says 'mid-first century CE'. Article gives 400 talents under Seuthes I per Thucydides (entry silent). The article's claim that the heartland became the Sapaean kingdom kept as stated.
Article's founding of Bergen c. 1070 is hedged by 'traditionally'/'said to'. Entry says c. 1050 birth, article c. 1050 but 'only 16 in 1066' implies c. 1050: consistent.

Article: orders to write the Historia 1110-1115; entry says c.1114; text avoids the start year. Article calls dates of death 'c. 1142' not stated; text says narrative ended 1141 only. Spelling 'Saint-Évroul' vs article 'Saint-Evroul'; changed to match entry's spelling.

Article calls Ordoño 'king of Galicia from 910'; entry same. Article says Garcia was 'firstborn' while also 'infant Garcia'; left out. Article has inconsistency on whether Fruela was 'eldest surviving brother'; used 'brother'.

Article lead dates the organisation 1933-1945; entry 1938-1945; text dates the Organisation proper to 1938 and the earlier office separately. 'Still stand' on Channel Islands not in article, omitted. Article says OT given its name by Hitler soon after 1933 (conflict with 1938); omitted.

SKIPPED: article under 300 words, mostly present-day industry and attractions; adds little to the entry Article only adds Kii Channel/Akashi Strait, port list, artificial islands, and that in antiquity the bay stretched almost to Kyoto with Naniwa a peninsula.

SKIPPED: article about 250 words of mostly lists (settlements, groups, departments); adds little to the entry Article calls it a south-east province; entry says eastern Chad. Article says the Ouaddai Empire lasted from early 16th century until 1911; Darfur refugees not in article.

Article states a 2020s crackdown by the Tajik government; omitted as a judgement on a present government. Article has conflicting statements on language branch (southeastern vs north-eastern); text says Eastern Iranian only.

Omitted: article's characterisations of the party as de facto one-party state, rankings of tenure, 'as of 2025' statements, semi-authoritarian descriptions, and recent family disputes. Article says 'After gaining independence from Britain, Singapore joined Malaysia in 1963' while entry says 'led into Malaysia 1963': consistent.

Article gives the princes' period as 1711–1716 to 1821 (varying), entry '1710s': text says 'from 1711 to 1716 onward' — rephrase if flagged. Article says 'From 1669 majority of dragomans'; entry says 'late 17th century': consistent. 'Principality of Samos' appears in entry, article says only 'Prince of Samos'.
Entry says he worked in Alexandria and Rhodes; article names only Alexandria, so Rhodes omitted.
Entry says Peace of Thorn 'returned Samogitia'; article says Knights agreed to resign claims during the two lifetimes; text uses article's wording. Article's 'Prussian Crusade' etc. unchanged.

Article says 'territories east of the Oder-Neisse under Polish and Soviet civil administration'; entry says 'Polish and Soviet administration': consistent. Article's lead says it addressed 'reparations' and 'prosecution of war criminals'; entry lists five principles; no conflict.
Article does not mention the Treaty of Trianon (entry does); text says Yugoslav troops took control on 12 August 1919 vs entry 'August 1919': consistent.

The article's body says nothing of Hudson's Bay or Rupert's Land beyond the lead, so they are not repeated. Mezzotint invention credited to Rupert is disputed in the article (Ludwig von Siegen); left out.
The article names two different amirs as his first owner; left out. Article says 'seventh Bahri Mamluk sultan'; not used.

Article dates the annexation of Sobrarbe and Ribagorza to 1043; the entry says around 1045, so no year given. Death of Gonzalo not mentioned in article; omitted. Article says Ramiro 'also became King of Pamplona', not used. Born 'before 1007' vs entry c. 1007: no birth year printed.
Article spells the father Chindaswinth; desc says Chindasuinth. Used the article's spelling.
Antisemitic content and Hitler cult are in the entry description; article body only mentions The Eternal Jew in passing, so not told here.
Article dates Pipes's Harvard teaching 1958-1996, matching entry.
Article gives length 192 km, entry says about 190; no length printed. Entry's 'fertile valley settled early' and Leinster/Osraige border dating not in article beyond 'historically'.
Article length 112 km vs entry about 110: not printed. Article gives AI770.2 annal; year 770 taken from the reference code, so possibly risky.
Entry says the 43 CE battle was two days near Rochester and describes the 1667 raid (de Ruyter, Royal Charles); the article gives neither, so only names and dates are used.
Article does not use the title margrave; entry does. Article's marriages are disputed; left out.
Pantheon dome line from entry not repeated. Article says 'candidate for the most durable building material', omitted.
Aslanduz date differs inside the article (19 vs 31 October 1812): only the month is given. Article says treaty gave 'most of modern Azerbaijan' in lead; body says khanates it held.

Article's lead says Austro-Hungarian official exonym for the entire Ukrainian population up to 1918; body says 1843 official name in Austrian Empire; both consistent. Kingdom of Hungary not specifically covered.
Article does not mention Florence expelling the Medici as a consequence (entry does); not repeated.
Article gives oil concessions in 1965; entry says exports began 1967: not stated. Article says Imam's revolt suppressed 1955 and 1957-59; entry says Jebel Akhdar War: dates left as in article.
Article gives baptism as 25 December 496 but also places Tolbiac around 497; entry says date variously 496-508, so no date printed. Death 13 January 533 not printed; entry gives 533.
Article spells compiler Kim Pusik in the lead and Kim Busik elsewhere; used Busik as the entry does. Entry says it favours Silla; article does not, so not stated.
Entry says the First Philippine Republic's government moved here in 1899; article does not say so, so omitted. Article dates the Death March 1942 and eruption 1991; years left out to keep clear.
Article does not mention Henry II's arbitration in 1177 (entry does), so omitted. Article gives Vitoria among 1181 towns, matching entry.
Article calls Sayyids Timurid vassals only under Khizr Khan; Mubarak Shah dropped allegiance. Muhammad Shah's death dated 1443 and 1445 in the article: no death year printed.
Article says Athens among Roman allies from the start; entry lists Achaean League from 198. Article's lead dates the Roman-Seleucid War 190 BC, later text 192 BC: dates left out.

Entry says Grotta Oscura tuff blocks and wall largely built early 4th c.; article says first wall of Cappellaccio tuff, Grotta Oscura used for repairs. Text follows the article for that detail and adds it as construction sequence; editor may check. 'Late Republic' as in article.
Article gives 'Shaykh Lutfallah Maysi al-'Amili (d.1622)'.
Entry says 'over 100,000'; article says over 125,000 (not printed).

SKIPPED: article has under 250 words of history; mostly modern municipal data, and it says only that Shiroishi Castle was the site of a battle in the Boshin War, differing from the entry's account of the alliance's headquarters
SKIPPED: article under 350 words, nearly all of it already in the description
Article text says 'for the last ten years access ... difficult', undated; reported as article gives it. Omitted IUCN ranking and prominence ranking per rules.
Article gives only lead and section openings. Entry says Lạng Sơn reverse in March 1885; article not exact on month, so 'later' used.

Article calls the pre-Roman settlement Illyrian; entry says Liburnian: left unlabeled. Article does not mention the conventus or a medieval bishopric (only the diocese's abandonment in 1828). Population list omitted except town figure.

Article says built 1259 to 1270 and also 'built in 1260'; entry says 1260s; text gives painting dated 1263-1270 only. Frescoes date: article gives 1263-1268 for various paintings; entry 'around 1265', not repeated.

Entry says 'has remained intermittently active'; article says eruptions until 2010, last 2013 - text follows article without contradicting. Article says 'more than half' uninhabitable vs entry 'southern half'; not printed.

Article does not mention Danelaw/Five Boroughs/918 or Burghley House history beyond Burghley Park; entry's claims not repeated. Wikipedia says town is 'south-westerly protrusion' of Lincolnshire. Population 19,701 in 2011 census.
Article inconsistent: Simonis fourth wife in one place, fifth in family list; Durrës taken 1284 vs 1296; Nogai episode dates: all left out.
Article gives reign end 1178 and Hattusa sack 1190 (some claim); entry says burned around 1180: all dates for the end left out.
Entry's name etymology (Cait, Norse) not repeated.

Article: Sviatopolk Prince of Turov 988-1015 vs 'put in charge at eight' (born c.980): consistent. Primary Chronicle dates first defeat to 1016 in one place and 1017 in another; text gives 1016 for Lubech as in chronicle account section; Thietmar's 1017 mentioned as his own claim.
Entry says Jeong Do-jeon killed 1398 and kept military control until death; neither is stated in the article so not repeated.
SKIPPED: article under 400 words with about 250 of substance, and it adds little beyond the entry; Nader's role is barely mentioned
Article says Tang established Anyang as capital and moved the Nine Tripod Cauldrons: not repeated as doubtful. Article dates c. 1670-1587 BC: omitted.
Article says 1915 presidency followed Arriaga's abrupt resignation.
Entry says about 235 km long; article gives 311 km with German Thaya and 235.4 without; text gives both with their meaning. Left out ranking (seventh longest in Czech Republic).
Entry dates it c. 524; article says 523: no year printed. Entry spells Theoderic; article Theodoric (article's spelling used).
Entry c. 380 – c. 315 BCE; article says born 378 or 377 and death around 320 BCE: no birth/death years printed.
Entry lists Macedonia among bordering areas and Haliacmon; article names Pieria, Imathia, Larissa, Chalkidiki and Aliakmon. Founding of Thessaloniki (entry: 315 BCE) not in article, left out.
Article puts the Housesteads pillar at 43-410 CE; Tacitus 98 CE agrees with entry.
Entry mentions the Aduatuci stronghold (Caesar, 57 BCE); not in article, left out.
Entry says founded early 1st century BCE; article says 70s BCE: no founding date printed.
Entry says Bugenhagen 'formerly rector'; article gives 1504 for his becoming rector. Article's notable-people table gives Bugenhagen 1505-1521 (slip), ignored.
Entry says convent founded 1202; article says founded 1202 but the deed of donation was signed 23 June 1203: the deed date was left out.

Entry says Elisu Sultanate from the 17th to 19th century; article says the capital moved to İlisu in the 18th century, so no century given for the sultanate. Entry says Lezgic group of Northeast Caucasian: not in article, left out.

Entry c. 1485; article says 1485 in lead but 'around 1487' in text: no birth year printed. Entry says he was killed during the siege; the article excerpt gives only the date 23 June 1565, so the text says 'died'.
Entry 525 BCE agrees. Inaros's execution date disputed in the article (left out).
Entry says a new government under Yusuf Lule took power; the article excerpt does not state Lule's accession, so Lule left out.
Left out recent leadership changes and 'as of' statements. Article says the Orange Order voted to end official links in March 2005.
Entry says court fled 1807; article says 1808: date left out.
Article gives the proclamation as 12 April 1801 'to coincide with Vaisakhi' yet says Vaisakhi fell on 11 April in 1801: day left out. Lahore (entry) not in article.
Entry says replaced after Roman conquest; article says extinct around the 1st century as speakers assimilated into the Roman sphere.
Article gives different years for his becoming leader and does not date the treaty: only 150 BCE used.
Longest river of southern Italy (entry) is not stated in the article, which says it is slightly longer than the Liri-Garigliano.
Article calls him Grand Prince of Vladimir; entry says Vladimir-Suzdal. Descendants being princes of Moscow not in article, left out.

Article gives May 1667 to May 1668; consistent with desc. Desc says France kept Lille; article agrees (Lille, Armentières, Bergues, Douai). Alliance signed 23 January 1668. Modern historians debate the Triple Alliance's role (left out).

Article calls the Five-Power Treaty the Washington Naval Treaty; desc mentions Weihaiwei promised back by Britain, not in article, so left out. Article says treaties were 'not renewed' and remained in effect fourteen years; I only used Japan ended participation 1936.
Article says William is sometimes counted as Duke William III or IV. Article says 'captained by Thomas FitzStephen' ambiguously; left out.

Article says the area was 'largely unpopulated until the 1800s'; desc says it lay in the Jurchen homeland with Eastern Xia's capital nearby in the early 13th century, so I did not repeat the 'unpopulated' claim. Article does not mention Korean settlement dates; desc says from the late 19th century; I only wrote the 1990 figure. Left out drug problem, 2009 and 2000 incidents.

Article says Zhang defeated Duan in 1920 supporting Cao Kun; fine. Announcement said he officially died 21 June 1928 (desc says June 1928; no conflict). Article's account of tillage: 20 to 35 million acres. 'Second Zhili-Fengtian War of 1924' from article (September 1924).

Desc: 'from 1849 until the early 20th century'; article says 1849 to 1923. Desc 'nearly half a million'; article gives estimated 450,000 and 'half a million' elsewhere; I used 450,000. Article also says 'over half the national population' of Indian ancestry vs 68 percent; used 68. Article says the 2 November ceremony honors jehaji bhai spirits; I wrote holiday only. 'Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi visit 1970' vs '1980s' wording unclear; left out.

SKIPPED: article is about 264 words in all and mostly repeats the entry; no 260 words of new substance (also its dates of death are speculative) Article adds: born January 1732, son of Tahmasp II and Shahpari Begum; Nader Khan deputy of state and viceroy; sent to Sabzevar; 1738 Reza Qoli Mirza ordered Tahmasp and sons killed by Mohammed Hosein Khan Qajar; dating May or June 1739 or 1740 speculative (Axworthy). Desc's Mughan plain assembly is not in the article.

Desc says proclaimed caliph in 909 (dates line 'proclaimed caliph 909'); article says proclaimed caliph and took power in Ifriqiya in January 910 while the conquest was 909. Left the proclamation date out. Article says the founder was the eleventh Imam of the Isma'ili branch; omitted. Article's section on later reign was truncated.

Desc says healed by the disciple Addai; article names Thaddeus of Edessa as the convert and the Doctrine of Addai as a source: I wrote Thaddeus. Dates: article c. 1st century BC to c. AD 50, desc 'd. c. 50 CE', 'early 1st century CE'; no dates printed beyond this. Mandylion mention is from article's sentence on 944. Letters to Tiberius: Khorenatsi calls Abgar king of Armenia; left out.
Article: 729-798 consistent with desc c. 729-798. Article says 'first Qadi al-Qudat'; desc same. Article's 'It is unclear' who appointed him; desc says Harun made him Grand Qadi - consistent.

Article says 910 BC battle; short article (372 words). Desc mentions a border treaty with Babylonia and tribute along the Khabur, which the article does not say; left out. Article gives 'Egypt under the Libyan 22nd Dynasty' trade link; omitted detail.

Article gives 811-783 BC; desc c. 811-783: consistent. Desc's Tell al-Rimah stele and 'possibly under mother's influence' compare article; I followed article. Very short article (286 words); text is near minimum.
